findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

An open package of raw ground beef was observed in a cooler drawer alongside an opened package of Ready-To-Eat (RTE) sliced cheese. Juices were observed throughout the bottom of the drawer. The PIC and cook were shown and the foods in the drawer discarded to correct. Education was conducted. Ensure that raw and RTE foods are stored so that cross contamination does not take place.

findings.title: Gloves used properly.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15 (A) Glove Use (A) if used, SINGLE-USE gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discard when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation. 

An employee was observed to handle a bluetooth speaker with their gloved hands and then handle ready for service meals and foods. Education was conducted and the PIC was instructed to educate staff as to when gloves should be changed. Change gloves whenever moving between tasks or whenever they may have become contaminated, and prior to handling foods.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. 

The hand sink next to the mop sink was blocked with a cart and broom. The PIC was shown and moved the items to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that all hand sinks are maintained accessible at all times.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

Two containers of milk in a standing cooler are observed with date marks of 3/17-3/31. This is incorrect. Seven day date marking from 3/17 would indicate that the milks should be used or discarded at the end of 3/23 (yesterday). The PIC was shown and education conducted with them and the employee nearby. The milks were discarded to correct. Ensure that date marking is conducted with correct procedures and followed. Ensure that staff is properly training on date marking to prevent future concerns.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day.

1) Two opened gallons of milk in the standing cooler at the end of the prep line are observed without date marking. Neither the PIC or the worker knew when the containers had been opened. 2) A gallon of milk is partially used and bares a date marking of 8/20. This indicates that it should have been discarded at the end of last night at the latest. All three containers of milk were discarded during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Education should trickle down to the employees working in this area to ensure that this situation does not repeat in the future.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

Several flies (at least 8-10) are observed by the mop sink and adjacent tanks. The PIC was shown and instructed to contact their pest control agency (EcoLab) for maintinance. They did mention that EcoLab had already been planning on starting a fly based plan in the facility. This should probably be pushed forward and implemented immediately. The normal follow-up schedule would land on a weekend and will be pushed back to the following Monday.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

A piece of equipment next to the grill is observed with encrusted food residue in the gaps/crack provided by cracked aluminum tape. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean and then re-seal the spaces prior to the next routine inspection. The PIC then indicated that this equipment was unused and a leftover from when Wahlburger’s was here. He stated that it would be discarded prior to the next inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

The hand sink next to the mop sink is observed pulling away from the wall, which is producing a gap that is not easily cleanable. The PIC was shown and instructed to repair prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that all facility equipment is maintained in good repair at all times.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

Th hand sink next to the mop sink is without paper towels at the beginning of this inspection. The PIC was notified and the paper towel dispenser refilled during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are supplied with needed supplies at all times.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

The soda gun in the bar area is observed stored submerged in the ice in the ice bin. The PIC was shown. This item is not regularly cleaned/sanitized on the outside or on the metal hose leading to it. Due to this this item should be stored outside of the ice (a Ready-to eat (RTE)) food to protect it from possible contamination. The gun was removed from the bin to correct.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

The wall behind the dish machine has a large amount of black mold on it, primarily to the right of the machine. The PIC was notified and had the surface cleaned during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Ensure the the facility is cleaned often enough so that the accumulation of filth does not take place.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. 

An employee drink is observed on the shelf above the prep cooler. The PIC was consulted and the drink discarded during this inspection to correct. Ensure that employee foods/drinks are stored seperately from foods or food contact surfaces to prevent possible contamination moving forward. It is preferred that storage is below and/or away from foods and food preparation areas.
